simple.meaning: בְּטֵל (bᵉṭêl) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to stop.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 6 times in Ezra, beginning at Ezra 4:21. The surrounding contexts include kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בְּטֵל (H989) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בְּטֵל (bᵉṭêl) / H989 is traced through Ezra 4:21, Ezra 4:23, Ezra 4:24, Ezra 5:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Make a decree now to cause these men to cease, and that this city not be built, until a decree is made by me.

majorEvents.label: Movement or place
majorEvents.evidenceText: Make a decree now to cause these men to cease, and that this city not be built, until a decree is made by me.

timeline.evidenceText: Make a decree now to cause these men to cease, and that this city not be built, until a decree is made by me.
Then when the copy of king Artaxerxes’ letter was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews, and made them to cease by force of arms.
Then work stopped on God’s house which is at Jerusalem. It stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
Then work stopped on God’s house which is at Jerusalem. It stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they didn’t make them cease, until the matter should come to Darius, and an answer should be returned by letter concerning it.

Moreover I make a decree what you shall do for these elders of the Jews for the building of this house of God: that of the king’s goods, even of the tribute beyond the River, expenses must be given with all diligence to these men, that they not be hindered.
